transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
A new court filing details the condition of the Tennessee woman who officials failed to execute earlier this week.
Attorneys for Christa Pike say she was placed on a ventilator and remained unconscious as hospital staff worked to save her life and clear the execution drug the state had administered.
Tony Gonzalez of member station WPLN reports.
Christa Pike's legal team wants the Tennessee Department of Corrections to preserve evidence and is asking a judge for help.
They're also citing several months of warnings they had provided about a blood disorder that would make it difficult to insert an IV line.
They were also concerned because prison staff had failed to insert a line during another lethal injection attempt in May.
Now they say that the drug pentobarbital could have been sent into Pike's arm instead of her vein.
Tennessee has struggled with lethal injections.
Four years ago, officials were found to have ignored protocols and mishandled drugs.
The state made changes, but concerns remained and the governor has now ordered another review.
For NPR News, I'm Tony Gonzalez in Nashville.
A federal judge has ordered all border-related construction to stop immediately in Texas' Big Bend region, including in Big Bend National Park.
As Marfa Public Radio's Mary Cantrell reports, the emergency injunction will remain in effect while a lawsuit moves forward.
The Center for Biological Diversity, a church restoration group, and a river guide are suing the federal government over its border wall plans.
The judge's order says the Big Bend region is not necessarily an area of high illegal entry, as federal waivers fast-tracking the project have claimed.
Anti-wall advocates, including Susan Hayes, celebrated outside of a federal courthouse in El Paso.
The government had no justification legally to issue the waivers in the first place. It's what we all knew. To say that there is an emergency with immigration or border security and the greater Big Bend is complete and utter yes.
If the Trump administration appeals, the case will go to the U.S. Supreme Court.
For NPR News, I'm Mary Cantrell in El Paso.
Mental health counselors are warning about the risks of prediction market sites, as NPR's Bobby Allen reports clinicians say problem gamblers are relapsing with apps like Kalshi and Polymarket.
Prediction market sites are surging. Kalshi's data shows the $60 billion bet on the platform last month was up 2,000 percent from 2025.
But unlike online sportsbooks like FanDuel and DraftKings, prediction markets do not honor so-called self-exclusion registries.
These are lists maintained by states that automatically ban gambling addicts from using betting sites.
Mental health experts say it is a loophole that many bettors are falling into after coming across Polymarket or Kalshi's ubiquitous ads.
Kalshi in a statement says it invests in responsible trading, including its own self-exclusion list.
But state officials say as long as Kalshi and Polymarket stay unlicensed by states, there are fewer consumer protections.
Bobby Allen, NPR News.
U.S. stocks rose near their record today. This is NPR.
Amazon says it's investing more than $1 billion over the next five years into communities where it operates data centers.
The money is for education, job training and water preservation projects.
It comes as data centers face growing backlash from consumers and politicians over water usage, noise pollution and local subsidies.
Animals may have evolved up to 200 million years before they show up on the fossil record, NPR's Ping Huang reports.
The oldest animal fossils are about 550 million years old.
Ross Anderson, a natural historian at Oxford University, says they're mostly shells and skeletons.
Presumably, animals had a history before this.
But because the animals then are soft and squishy, it's actually really hard to get them preserved as fossils.
New analysis by Anderson and his colleagues suggests that animals came long before that when much of the earth was a ball of ice.
Looking at evidence from sites around the world, they calculated the maximum age for the origin of animals back some 750 million years ago.
These were probably sponge-like critters that lived on the seafloor.
While this research doesn't prove animals existed that long ago,
Anderson says it gives them a direction in which to dig for evidence.
The paper is published in the Journal of Science Advances. Ping Huang, NPR News.
Major League Baseball introduced robot umpires this year, allowing hitters, catchers and pitchers to have a computer automatically review balls and strikes.
Now that the regular season is over, robot umpires overturned 54 percent of challenged calls.
The Cincinnati Reds benefited the most from overturns, and catchers were more successful than batters.
This is NPR News.
